study.question: Does removing the explicit within-prefix behavior-count prior from normalized target-aware attention improve joint use of the supplied category/brand/action/age histories at fixed capacity? Observation: successful static/pool/DIN AUCs are 0.6050036145/0.6102261137/0.6133619861. DIN-minus-pool AUC is +0.0031358724 overall, +0.0026743907 on category-match-present (2,516,922 samples; 129,821 positive, 2,387,101 negative) and +0.0002617450 on category-match-absent (717,129; 29,616 positive, 687,513 negative); absent-slice Logloss still improves 0.1722469945 to 0.1720905077. The two slice gains are exploratory, single-seed observations, not evidence for a query bottleneck. Source inspection shows all event types share one softmax, so for equal per-event scores type mass is proportional to its visible count. Marginal behavior-presence counts do not establish within-history dominance. The frozen input boundary makes a count correction more directly testable than inventing extra history or asserting contextual-query failure.
study.hypothesis: If behavior multiplicity is partly an exposure-frequency nuisance rather than useful interest intensity, replacing w_j proportional to exp(s_j) with w_j proportional to exp(s_j)/n[type_j] can expose complementary low-count actions without increasing capacity. For present type a, its total mass becomes mean_j_in_a(exp(s_j)) normalized across present types, retaining target-aware within-type and between-type evidence. This is not fixed equal mass per type unless per-event scores are equal; pooling is the equal-mass special case. This may help mixed-type histories, including category-absent cases, but neither the prevalence of harmful dominance nor predictive utility has been measured. The opposite hypothesis, that frequency is useful intensity, is credible and consistent with the motivation in original DIN.

nearest_work.source_ref: https://arxiv.org/html/1706.06978v4 section 4 Eq.3 and following normalization discussion (v4)
nearest_work.difference: Inherit target-aware local activation from the supplied adapter. Original DIN deliberately omits softmax to preserve interest intensity; the supplied adapter uses normalized attention. The candidate retains normalization and tests a type-count prior instead. This is not an exact DIN replication, and the primary text is counterevidence to assuming all frequency is nuisance.

HMAR uses behavior-masked self-attention followed by sequence-wide self-attention and behavior-frequency indicators. This experiment has no behavior-specific learned encoders, sequence transformer, frequency-feature embedding, or auxiliary objective; it isolates a fixed correction in the existing target-aware readout. Behavior separation is established prior work, not a new priority claim.

MATN combines behavior-specific interaction views, cross-behavior attention, customized memory transforms and gated aggregation. The proposed correction uses only the supplied causal event prefix in the existing field model, without global interaction vectors or new memory. Task, information and evaluation differ; no result transfers automatically.

The primary equations use within-behavior masked attention and learned aggregation after local/global graph routing. Here group evidence is exactly the mean exponential score through a fixed inverse-count correction, without graphs, routing, spectral features or learned group heads. This is a narrower parameter-free contrast, not a claim to have invented hierarchical behavior aggregation. General log-frequency attention correction novelty remains unverified.
Primary publisher retrieval was blocked. No detailed comparison or full-paper verification is asserted. Further nearest-work verification is needed before any novelty claim.

study.proposed_difference: One fixed operation: subtract log(max(1,n_a)) from each DIN event score for its supplied behavior type a before the same masked softmax. Counts ignore padding and use only the supplied prefix. For mean pooling divide each event weight by n_a then renormalize over valid events. This forms a full 2x2 correction-by-target-scoring factorial in four standalone modules. All learned modules, embedding sharing, shapes and initialization order remain identical to the baseline. This is mechanism-distinct from the provided global-softmax adapter; scientific novelty is unverified. Unknowns include host category_match slice definition, original missing/unseen category encoding, action/time joint distributions, and readiness-audit details. No protocol or scoring change is proposed.
predictions: Primary predeclared contrast: count_corrected_din minus ordinary_din full-population validation ROC-AUC > 0 under matched seed 42; require same-sign mean paired effect on seeds 42/43/44 when resources permit. Report raw per-seed effects and variation, not significance from a single run. Report unweighted Logloss separately, including tradeoffs.

Mechanistic prediction at fixed scores: equal scores yield 1/K mass per present type after correction versus n_a/N ordinarily; within-type event odds are unchanged. Single-type and empty histories have unchanged weights/summaries at a shared checkpoint up to rounding. Retrained single-type predictions can change because parameters were learned on all histories.

Factorial prediction: positive difference-in-differences indicates target-aware scoring complements count correction; a shared gain in pooling and DIN instead supports generic balancing. Neither requires category-absent slice gain, and population AUC remains the selection metric.

Candidate diagnostics on only the host first-512 validation batch report supplied event totals, per-type presence, mixed/single/empty counts, pv-share>=0.90 mixed count, and ordinary versus corrected per-type mass and summary L2 changes at the SAME checkpoint. These are label-free descriptive measurements with denominators; they do not estimate full-population predictive benefit or positive/negative counts.

Use host frozen history-length, hour, behavior-presence, frequency and category-match slices with supplied sample/positive/negative counts; mark absent or insufficient slices and do not invent joint-slice class counts. Visible category/brand diagnostic matches exclude ID zero and use only supplied events; they are explicitly distinct from the unverified host category_match definition. Any new full-data joint slice or user-cluster bootstrap requires an authorized later interface and must be charged to budget.

Parameter count should remain 17,130,275 for all four cells under supplied meta. Measure allocated GPU seconds, total wall time, examples processed, peak memory and end-to-end throughput/p50/p95 using host receipts; parameter equality alone makes no equal-compute or speed claim.
falsifiers: Positive corrected attention mass to rare actions without positive population AUC is not predictive support; a negative repeatable correction effect favors retention of behavior multiplicity or a different aggregation design.
A nonreproducing ordinary DIN/pool bridge invalidates attribution until implementation/configuration/sampling discrepancies are explained; do not silently tune or change the contract.

Any intervention-induced change of shared-checkpoint weights on one-type histories beyond rounding, nonzero padding/empty summary, nonfinite logits, or wrong shape is an implementation failure, not a scientific refutation.

No mixed-type support or negligible counterfactual change in the diagnostic sample makes the proposed mechanism poorly exposed there, not disproven globally. Absence of predictive history or coarsened/truncated fields can also prevent gains.

A gain confined to one seed or an exploratory slice, worsening population ranking, or an unaffordable measured cost fails the stated selection criterion; preserve every null, negative, timed-out and failed receipt.
alternative_explanations: The absent-category slice already has higher absolute AUC; smaller DIN-minus-pool gain need not imply harder data or a deficient query. Different prevalence, user frequency and ranking opportunity can explain it.

History truncation to 128 events, category/brand summation, missing/unseen fields, action/recency correlations, insufficient predictive history, optimizer trajectory or seed variation may dominate the observed gap.

Behavior counts may encode real interest intensity; count correction could discard useful evidence or overweight noisy rare actions. Original DIN explicitly motivates preserving intensity, and behavior presence alone does not measure dominance.

Any correction gain might be generic balancing/regularization rather than better target relevance; the pooling factorial contrast addresses this. It does not separate every action-versus-recency confound or prove causal mediation.

The static snapshot as-of dates are undocumented in the host contract, limiting production point-in-time interpretation. Different tasks/splits and richer item identities in primary prior work prevent automatic transfer claims.
